description: An ordered procedure for sewing a worked headband onto a vellum or cord core at the head of a book, from setting the boards and book in the press through forming and beading the silk, tying down at intervals, and finishing off the ends.
name: working a headband on a vellum slip

en: working a headband on a vellum slip

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1901), Chapter XI, p.147. Internet Archive.
Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (D. Appleton, 1901), Internet Archive

steps.description: Ease the boards on the slips and pull them down so the top edges sit flush with the top edge of the leaves, preventing the silk catching on projecting edges.
Stand the book in a finishing press, fore-edge toward the worker and tilted forward, with light coming from the left across the work.
Pass a silk-threaded needle in at the head through the centre of the first section after the endpapers and out at the back below the kettle stitch, leaving about two-thirds of the silk.
Re-insert the needle in the same place and draw through to leave a loop, then seat the core in the loop with its end projecting slightly to the left, pinning it with a second vertical needle.
Carry the back strand over the core, cross it with the front strand under the core, and pull tight from the back to form the first crossings of the bead.
Repeat the crossings, keeping the bead tight and well down on the leaves, watching that the core does not shift.
Tie the band down frequently by passing the needle between the leaves and out at the back below the kettle stitch, then resume the crossings; a tie-down about every third pass keeps it secure.
Work the band along to the endpapers, finish with a double tie-down, draw the front strand under the core to the back, then cut, fray, and paste both silk ends flat on the back.
Trim the core ends close to the silk and check the length by compressing the sections with thumb and finger; shorten the band if it buckles.
